entities.summary: Shō Toku was the final king of the First Shō dynasty of the Ryukyu Kingdom, ruling from 1461 until his death. Ostensibly the son of the prior king Shō Taikyū, he may have taken power through force. He is portrayed as a cruel and violent ruler in the later official histories of the kingdom, forcing ministers into hiding and subduing the island of Kikaijima through a costly and brutal military campaign. He was a patron of the Japanese deity Hachiman, adopting his symbol as a royal crest, taking the divine name "Hachiman-no-Aji", and building the Asato-Hachimangū shrine to him near Naha after his conquests.
